methods.name: Peer-Median

methods.rationale: 7 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Percepto is a Series C-stage autonomous systems company in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The company has raised $128M to date. The valuation universe consists of seven private-sector peers including Waymo, Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, and Nuro; no public comparables exist in this narrow subsegment.

A peer-median approach proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum sample thresholds (zero same-stage peers, two adjacent-stage peers identified, below the required three-datapoint floor). A stage-progression method was therefore applied as the primary triangulation approach. Using total raised ($128M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series C-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 1.7x yields an implied valuation of $218M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $185M (low) to $250M (high), centered on a median of $218M. This range reflects a single methodological pillar, which represents a material limitation. Key uncertainties include the applicability of the 1.7x multiplier to Percepto's specific risk profile and growth trajectory relative to sector peers, and the absence of publicly traded comparables to anchor valuation multiples. Expansion of the peer dataset or access to transaction multiples in the autonomous systems space would strengthen conviction in this range.
